explain.say: First the damaged blood vessel tightens to slow the flow. Then platelets, tiny cell fragments in blood, touch the torn wall, turn sticky and pile up into a loose plug.

explain.say: The platelets and the damaged tissue set off a chain of clotting proteins. At the end, a protein called fibrinogen is turned into long threads of fibrin that weave a net over the plug.

faq.a: Platelets are tiny pieces of cells in your blood. When a vessel is damaged they become sticky, cling to the edges and to each other, and form the first plug. They also release chemicals that start the clotting chain.
Fibrin is a stringy protein. Clotting turns a dissolved protein called fibrinogen into fibrin threads, which form a mesh that traps blood cells and makes the clot solid.
asks: Tell me about the fibrin net

faq.q: Why doesn't blood clot inside us all the time?
faq.a: Healthy vessel walls are smooth and release substances that stop platelets sticking. Clotting only switches on where a wall is damaged, and other proteins keep the clot from spreading.
asks: Why does blood stay runny in your veins?

faq.a: A scab is a dried blood clot on the skin. It seals the wound against germs while new skin grows underneath, then falls off when the skin is ready.

faq.q: How long does it take blood to clot?
faq.a: In a small cut, bleeding usually slows within a few minutes as the platelet plug and fibrin net form.

facts: Platelets are cell fragments made in the bone marrow from large cells called megakaryocytes.
Clotting converts the soluble protein fibrinogen into insoluble fibrin threads.

quiz.say: What forms the net that makes a blood clot solid?
quiz.show: What forms the net that makes a blood clot solid?
quiz.why: Fibrin threads weave a mesh that traps red cells and platelets into a firm clot.

wrong.1: White blood cells fight germs; they do not make the clot net.
wrong.2: Plasma is the liquid part of blood; the clot needs solid threads.
